<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par124 />{{GHGheb|text=וּבְבָֽתֵּי כְלָאִים|translate=and in prison houses}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=22}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=1}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵיֽ־לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים|translate=two tables of stone}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=לֻחֹת אֶ֫בֶן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=14|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=3}}, &c. {{GHGheb|text=עַמֵּי הָֽאֲרָצוֹת|translate=the people of the country}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=14}}; so perhaps {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי אֵלִים|translate=sons of God}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=7|hidebook=1}} (according to others ''sons of gods''); or finally even

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|r}}
(''c'') By using the plural of the ''nomen rectum'';<ref>Cf. Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 482.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית אָבוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=1|verse=2}}, 4 ff., &c., as plur. of {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית אָב}} ''father’s house, family''; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית הַבָּמוֹת|translate=the houses of the high places}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=29}} (also {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽתֵּי הַבָּמוֹת}} 23:19); {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית עֲצַבֵּיהֶם|translate=the houses of their idols}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=31|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=24}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=25}} ''the head of Oreb and Zeeb'', i.e. the heads, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|s}}
Rem. When a substantive (in a distributive sense) with a suffix refers back to a plural, the singular form of the substantive suffices, since the idea of plurality is already adequately expressed by the suffix, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פִּימוֹ|translate=os}} (for ''ora'') ''eorum'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְמִינָם|translate=their right hand}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=8}} [so in the English RV.], for ''hands''.<section end=par124 />

<section begin=par125 />{{GHGpar-heading|125|Determination of Nouns in general. Determination of Proper Names}}

<div style="font-size: small; text-align: center;">Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 466 ff.</div>

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|a}}
'''1.''' A noun may either be determinate in itself, as a proper name or pronoun (see below, ''d'' and ''i''), or be made so by its context. In the latter case, the determination may be effected either by prefixing the article (see § 126), or by the connexion of the noun (in the construct state) with a following determinate genitive, and consequently also (according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}) by its union with a pronominal suffix ({{GHGpar|127|a}}). It is to be taken as a fundamental rule, that the determination can only be effected in ''one'' of the ways here mentioned; the article cannot be prefixed to a proper name, nor to a noun followed by the genitive, nor can a proper name be used in the construct state. Deviations from this rule are either only apparent or have arisen from a corruption of the text.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|b}}
Rem. Only in a few passages is a noun made expressly ''indeterminate'' by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} in the sense of our indefinite article; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=53}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, 12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (in 8:13 {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד קָדוֹשׁ}} i.e. ''one'', viz. ''a holy one'', is opposed to another).

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|c}}
It is further to be noticed, that in Hebrew the phenomenon sometimes occurs, which the Arab grammarians call ''indeterminateness for the sake of amplification''; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=8}} ''and he shall flee'' {{GHGheb|text=מִפְּנֵי־חֶ֫רֶב|translate=from a sword}}, i.e. ''from an irresistible sword'' (God’s sword); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיָד}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁם}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=3|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=such a woman}}, without doubt to be referred to the Gomer mentioned in cap. 1;<section end=par125 /><noinclude>
